# Hydra — llms.txt (AI-agent digest, ~1.5K tokens)

> Header-only C++20 arbitrary-precision integer library. One class, `hydra::Hydra`,
> with a tiered runtime representation: Small (≤64-bit, register-speed, no heap),
> Medium (65–192-bit, inline payload), Large (heap limbs). Sign-magnitude signed
> arithmetic. Variable-time by design — public-input workloads only (verification,
> VDFs, primality), never secret keys. MIT. Repo: github.com/henry-filgueiras/hydra

## Read this first, not the big docs
- `DIRECTORS_NOTES.md` (~80K tokens) = full design history: Current Canon (present
  truth) + Resolved Dragons (append-only experiment log incl. null results). Grep
  its `### ` headers; read only the section you need.
- `perf_snapshot.md` = current benchmark tables. `CLAUDE.md` = repo working rules
  (update notes + commit per exchange, never push). `ROADMAP.md` = moonshot
  tracks (A=adoption, B=perf, C=trust/meta) with dependency graph + statuses.
- All implementation is in `hydra.hpp` (~4600 lines). `hydra.cpp` is a stub TU.

## Public API (namespace hydra)
- Construction: `Hydra{int/uint any width}` (implicit), `Hydra{"‑123…"}` (decimal
  string), `Hydra::from_limbs(const uint64_t*, uint32_t)` (LSB-first magnitude).
- Operators: `+ - * / % << >> & | ^ ~ == <=> +=` etc. Signed semantics; division
  truncates toward zero; shifts are sign-magnitude (`x<<n == x*2^n`, `x>>n ==
  x/2^n` toward zero: `-3>>1 == -1`, NOT arithmetic shift); `&|^` throw
  std::domain_error on negative operands; `~x` = −(x+1). Shift counts unsigned.
- Methods: `.divmod(b)` → `{quotient, remainder}`, `.div_u64(u)`, `.mod_u64(u)`
  (zero-heap), `.to_string()`, `.is_zero()`, `.is_negative()`, `.negate()`,
  `.fits_u64()` (true iff value ∈ [0, 2^64)), `.to_u64()` (throws
  std::overflow_error unless fits_u64 — negatives never fit), `.limb_view()` →
  `{const uint64_t* ptr, uint32_t count}` (LSB-first magnitude; count 0 = zero).
- Free functions: `abs, gcd, extended_gcd` (→ `{gcd,x,y}` Bézout), `pow_mod(base,
  exp, mod)` (Montgomery for odd mod ≤4096 bits, else naive; throws on mod≤0 or
  exp<0), `pow_mod_batch(span<const Hydra> bases, exp, mod)` → vector (shared
  exp+mod verification shape; fused 2-lane ladder, 1.33×@2048b/1.38×@4096b
  native throughput, per-element pow_mod semantics + fallbacks), `isqrt` (floor,
  throws on negative), `is_perfect_square`,
  `is_probable_prime(n, extra_mr_rounds=0)` (Baillie–PSW: trial<256 → MR base 2 →
  strong Lucas/Selfridge; exact <2^64, no known counterexample), `next_prime`.
- Literal: `123_h`.

## Internals map (detail::, hydra.hpp)
- Kernels: `add/sub/mul_limbs`, `mul_3x3/4x4/8x8`, `mul_karatsuba` (≥32 limbs via
  `mul_general`), `divmod_knuth_limbs` (Knuth D), `shl/shr_limbs`,
  `divmod_u64_limbs`.
- Magnitude cores: `detail::divmod_magnitude` (sign-free |u|÷|v| on raw spans —
  Hydra::divmod's general case delegates), `detail::isqrt_magnitude` (isqrt
  delegates). `detail::MagnitudeView` = borrowed-limb view, wasm-import probe
  ARCHIVED 2026-07-11 (≤3% e2e — compute ≥100× the import copy; the real
  boundary tax is JS-side BigInt extract). Don't add view variants to more ops.
- Montgomery (pow_mod engine): dispatch is FIOS (dual-row CIOS,
  `montgomery_mul_fios`) at every k=1..64; squaring uses
  `montgomery_sqr_fios_halved` (cross-term halving, ~1.5k² MACs) for k≤32
  (`HALVED_SQR_MAX_K`), sqr-as-mul above. Sliding window is adaptive: W=6 for
  exponents ≥512 bits, else W=4 (`HYDRA_POWMOD_WINDOW` forces fixed W for
  sweeps). Retired-but-callable references (tests/AB only, NOT dispatched):
  `montgomery_mul{,_fused,_sos,_karatsuba}`.
- Key invariants: results always normalized to smallest tier; zero is Small,
  non-negative, limb count 0; kernels are magnitude-only, sign applied by
  operators; `work` buffers k+2 limbs for FIOS. Representation state
  (meta/payload) is PRIVATE; repo tests/benches fabricate states via
  `detail::TestAccess` (not stable API). sizeof(Hydra)=32, alignof=8
  (static_asserted — "32-byte object", never alignas(32)).

## Performance identity (Apple M5 Pro, 2026-07)
- pow_mod: ~7.3 µs @256b (parity with GMP), 1.80 ms @2048b (1.65× GMP),
  14.5 ms @4096b (1.94× GMP); 3–4.5× faster than Boost cpp_int everywhere.
- WebAssembly: whole suite passes unchanged; beats mini-gmp 5.0–7.4×, Boost
  2.6–3.9× in-browser (GMP has no wasm asm; LLVM-only pipeline, see below).
  Small ops ≈1.1–1.3× native u64.
- npm package `pkg/` (hydra-bignum): bigint→bigint powMod/modInverse/primality
  API (extra MR rounds: integer in [0, 64], RangeError outside — never
  clamped/wrapped); beats native JS BigInt 2.6×@256b…1.3×@2048b, loses
  0.8×@4096b (V8 is subquadratic). Build: `scripts/wasm_pkg.sh --test`.
  Publish = human step.

## Build / test / bench
- Tests: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug && cmake --build build --target
  hydra_test -j && ./build/hydra_test` (Debug = ASan+UBSan; 1250 checks). Release
  mirror in `build-rel`. CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — native matrix + header
  self-sufficiency + wasm (emsdk PINNED 6.0.2) + npm packed-tarball install gate
  (`scripts/npm_pack_test.sh` — in-tree pkg tests alone once masked a tarball
  missing its .wasm).
- Benchmarks: `./build-rel/bench_pow_mod --runs 6 --md` (min-of-medians +
  cross-run CV — ALWAYS use --runs, never single-run deltas; noise ±10% at small
  widths). Probes in `bench/probe_*.cpp` (kernel + "pow_mod cadence" layers).
  Provenance: attach `scripts/capture_benchmark_env.sh -- <bench cmd>` output
  (git SHA, toolchain, GMP/OpenSSL + brew versions, flags) to every new table.
  Retired-backend A/B probe: `-DHYDRA_BENCH_MONT_BACKENDS=ON` →
  `bench_mont_backends` (opt-in, never in CI).
- wasm: `scripts/wasm_bootstrap.sh` (toolchain), `wasm_bench.sh` (shootout),
  `wasm_demo.sh [--serve]` (in-browser demo, `demo/`), `wasm_vdf_demo.sh
  [--serve]` (flagship Wesolowski VDF demo, `demo/vdf/` — evaluate/prove/verify
  core in vdf.mjs over the pkg API, node suite `demo/vdf/test.mjs` in CI,
  deploys at /vdf/; 2048b·T=2²⁰: eval 2.5s, verify 2.1ms). mini-gmp is fetched,
  never vendored (LGPL). Bench builds are wasm-EH-free (-fwasm-exceptions costs ~15%);
  hydra_test needs -fwasm-exceptions.

## Hard-won rules (cost real time to learn — don't relearn)
- Re-sweep every dispatch threshold whose other side changed (paid out twice).
- Kernel-probe wins can invert e2e; the k+2-limb fused accumulator locality is
  the decisive Montgomery invariant; 2k-limb intermediates lose under cadence.
- asm/PGO/__restrict at these kernels: all measured null on M5 Pro — don't retry
  without a structural change (see Resolved Dragons). The structural change that
  DOES work: fused 2-lane FIOS = 1.5× kernel throughput → pow_mod_batch LANDED
  at 1.33×@2048b e2e (wasm null; call-level null; 4 lanes ≈ 2; under fusion
  sqr-as-mul beats fused halved-sqr; squarings must flush in pointer-invariant
  RUNS — per-call dispatch costs ~20%/mul, see montgomery_sqr_run_xL).
- Browser timing: performance.now clamps to 100µs–1ms → batch ≥15ms per sample.
- emcc's post-link `wasm-opt -O2` PESSIMIZES the kernels (+39%@256b…+60%@4096b
  with multiple exports). Ship LLVM-O2 only: `-g` build + passes-free
  `wasm-opt --strip-dwarf` (see wasm_pkg.sh, wasm_bench.sh). Shootout re-benched
  2026-07-10 under the fixed pipeline; the demo/ build + its recorded results +
  README screenshots still use the old default pipeline (conservative).
